query_text: Does it matter what we eat?

content.text:
Yes—it matters a lot, though you don’t need to eat “perfectly.”

What we eat affects:

- **Energy and mood** — meals with enough protein, fiber, and healthy fats tend to keep blood sugar steadier.
- **Long-term health** — diet influences risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, some cancers, and osteoporosis.
- **Gut health** — fiber-rich foods feed beneficial gut bacteria.
- **Body weight and muscle** — calories matter, but so do protein, food quality, sleep, and activity.
- **Brain function** — your brain needs steady fuel and nutrients like omega-3s, B vitamins, iron, iodine, and magnesium.
- **Immune function** — under-eating or lacking key nutrients can make the body less resilient.

A simple way to think about it:

**Most of the time, aim for:**
- Vegetables and fruits
- Beans, lentils, whole grains, potatoes, oats, brown rice, etc.
- Protein: fish, eggs, yogurt, tofu, poultry, lean meats, beans
- Healthy fats: nuts, olive oil, avocado, seeds
- Water most of the time

**Limit, without obsessing:**
- Sugary drinks
- Highly processed snack foods
- Excess alcohol
- Frequent large portions of fried or very salty foods

The big picture matters more than any single meal. A generally balanced pattern over weeks and months is what makes the difference.
